# stripe_billing_credit_grant (Resource)

Billing credits given to a customer. `terraform destroy` voids the grant, because Stripe cannot delete one: the unused credits can no longer be applied, and the grant stays in the account. Only `expires_at` and `metadata` can change after creation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_customer" "acme" {
  email = "billing@acme.example"
}

resource "stripe_billing_credit_grant" "welcome" {
  name     = "Welcome credit"
  customer = stripe_customer.acme.id
  category = "promotional"

  amount = {
    type = "monetary"
    monetary = {
      currency = "usd"
      value    = 2500
    }
  }

  applicability_config = {
    scope = {
      price_type = "metered"
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `amount` (Attributes) Amount of this credit grant. Changing it replaces the resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--amount))
- `applicability_config` (Attributes) Configuration specifying what this credit grant applies to. We currently only support `metered` prices that have a [Billing Meter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/billing/meter) attached to them. Changing it replaces the resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--applicability_config))

### Optional

- `category` (String) The category of this credit grant. It defaults to `paid` if not specified. Possible values: `paid`, `promotional`. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `customer` (String) ID of the customer receiving the billing credits. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `customer_account` (String) ID of the account representing the customer receiving the billing credits. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `effective_at` (Number) The time when the billing credits become effective-when they're eligible for use. It defaults to the current timestamp if not specified. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `expires_at` (Number) The time when the billing credits expire. If not specified, the billing credits don't expire.
- `metadata` (Map of String) Set of key-value pairs that you can attach to an object. You can use this to store additional information about the object (for example, cost basis) in a structured format.
- `name` (String) A descriptive name shown in the Dashboard. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `priority` (Number) The desired priority for applying this credit grant. If not specified, it will be set to the default value of 50. The highest priority is 0 and the lowest is 100. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created` (Number) Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the object.
- `livemode` (Boolean) If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
- `test_clock` (String) ID of the test clock this credit grant belongs to.
- `updated` (Number) Time at which the object was last updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
- `voided_at` (Number) The time when this credit grant was voided. If not present, the credit grant hasn't been voided.

Required:

- `value` (Number) A positive integer representing the amount.

<a id="nestedatt--applicability_config--scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `applicability_config.scope`

Optional:

- `price_type` (String) The price type that credit grants can apply to. We currently only support the `metered` price type. This refers to prices that have a [Billing Meter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/billing/meter) attached to them. Cannot be used in combination with `prices`. Possible values: `metered`.
- `prices` (Attributes List) The prices that credit grants can apply to. We currently only support `metered` prices. This refers to prices that have a [Billing Meter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/billing/meter) attached to them. Cannot be used in combination with `price_type`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--applicability_config--scope--prices))

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import stripe_billing_credit_grant.welcome credgr_test_123
```
